transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I wanted to call this meeting because we have twenty-four drums of solvent waste from the recent line-cleaning operation sitting in the hazardous-waste cage, and our temporary storage permit expires on Friday. We need to finalize a disposition plan before that deadline. As per our waste-closeout policy, the waste coordinator and production supervisor need to review their current records with me before we can approve any disposition. Can we start by confirming the current status of the drums and whether the material meets the approved recovery specification?

transcript.text: I received the laboratory classification report yesterday. It shows that 15 drums meet the approved solvent-recovery specification, 3 drums fail the water-content limit and must go to hazardous-waste incineration, and the remaining 6 drums were not classified in that report. A laboratory-system outage kept the report from being uploaded to the waste log, which is why it hasn't been visible in our records until now.

transcript.text: Thanks, Jon. Before we go further on those 6 unclassified drums, I need to flag something important. My completed batch-genealogy review identifies those 6 drums as being from lot VX-204. They contain residual catalyst and must be retained on site for exactly 30 days for possible process investigation rather than being sent for treatment. I haven't entered the hold tags in the production system yet, but I'm going to need to do that. So for disposition planning, we're really looking at three categories: 15 drums for solvent recovery, 3 drums for hazardous-waste incineration, and 6 drums on a 30-day on-site hold. We'll need to make sure the waste-closeout form reflects separate commitments for each of those disposition categories, and the treatment manifest should cover the total number of drums actually removed from the cage — which would be the 18 going to recovery and incineration, not the 6 on hold.

transcript.text:
Thank you both for the updates. Let me summarize what I'm hearing for the record:

- 15 drums meet the approved solvent-recovery specification and are approved for solvent recovery disposition.
- 3 drums fail the water-content limit and must go to hazardous-waste incineration.
- 6 drums from lot VX-204 contain residual catalyst and must be retained on-site for 30 days for process investigation, per Priya's batch-genealogy review. Priya, please make sure those hold tags get entered in the production system as soon as possible.

For the waste-closeout form, we'll need three separate disposition commitments: one for the 15 drums to solvent recovery, one for the 3 drums to hazardous-waste incineration, and one for the 6 drums on a 30-day on-site hold. The treatment manifest should cover the 18 drums actually being removed from the cage for off-site treatment — the 15 to recovery and 3 to incineration — not the 6 on hold.

Before I can finalize and sign off on the closeout form, I need to confirm with both of you: Jon, will the laboratory classification report be uploaded to the waste log to close that documentation gap? And Priya, will the hold tags be entered before we submit? Once those items are confirmed and our records review is complete, I can approve the disposition.
transcript.speaker: A1
